heroHeadline: Day 79: ACLED — CJNG Shows Zero Fracture Post-Mencho; El Sapo Hunt Continues; 30 Days to FIFA World Cup; CJNG Reinforcing Michoacán Alliances with Los Viagras
heroSubtitle: Day 79 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). ACLED ASSESSMENT (May 12, 2026): ACLED's Latin America chief analyst finds zero evidence the CJNG has fractured 79 days post-Mencho — organization showing 'tactical containment' and actively reinforcing alliances with Los Viagras in Michoacán. Companion El Imparcial analysis: CJNG franchise model enables autonomous cell resilience regardless of leadership disruption. EL SAPO HUNT — DAY 79: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán 'El Sapo' (CJNG military chief) remains at large as Mexico's Federal Security Cabinet top-priority CJNG enforcement target (named May 3). FGR protected witness testimony (former FARC Front 30 escort): 'when El Mencho is gone, El 090 will take it all.' POST-EL CHUCKY MANZANILLO VOID (Day 3): Port of Manzanillo CJNG plaza command in transition — no successor publicly identified; embedded port relationships intact; El 03's Grupo Élite expected to designate replacement within 1–2 weeks. DECAPITATION CAMPAIGN — 79-DAY LEDGER: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Doble R (arrested March 11), El Jardinero (arrested April 27, formally charged Altiplano May 4), El Güero Conta (arrested April 27), El Cabo (arrested May 7), El Chucky/plaza boss (arrested May 9). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials detained. SUCCESSION BINARY: El 03 (Juan Carlos Valencia González, financial wing, confirmed CJNG leader — El País, April 6) vs. El Sapo (military wing, at large). ACLED's no-fracture finding supports O3 consolidation narrative even as El Sapo's continued freedom sustains internal military-wing tension. PLAN KUKULKAN — 30 DAYS: Mexico's FIFA World Cup 2026 security strategy now 30 days from June 11 opening match. Guadalajara (Akron Stadium) hosts 4 group-stage matches; Mexico's 130,000-person nationwide security deployment continues. QUINTUPLE BILATERAL PRESSURE TRACK — MAXIMUM STRESS: (1) CIA-Chihuahua sovereignty deadlock (Maru Campos declined April 28 Senate hearing — 'institutional crisis'); (2) DOJ SDNY indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya + 9 officials ('temporary leave' since May 2); (3) Sheinbaum's 'irrefutable proof' extradition standard (May 6); (4) U.S. State Dept formal review of all 53 Mexican consulates (May 7–8); (5) ongoing CJNG interdiction framework. Trump May 7: 'if they're not gonna do the job, we will' — maximum rhetorical escalation point. KEY METRICS: (1) El Sapo capture/elimination before June 11; (2) Manzanillo successor designation and port disruption durability; (3) bilateral sovereignty crisis impact on operational coordination; (4) 130,000-person security deployment deterrence through World Cup opening.
